AWAR D 1.
Proceedings in the present case have arisen by filing of DAR in this Tribunal in FIR No.208/2023 of PS Vivek Vihar registered under section 279/304A IPC.

Facts deducible from the DAR are that on 24.05.2023 at about 1.25 a.m. in the night, deceased was going for his welding work in Vivek Vihar for construction work on flyover along with other co-workers.

In the meanwhile offending vehicle bearing registration no. HR-38W-1670 came from Anand Vihar side at a very high speed and being driven in a rash and negligent manner hit the iron angle on which deceased was sitting and doing welding work with great force.
As a result neck of the deceased crushed between two angles and he received fatal injuries.
Such was the impact of the accident that head of the deceased was severed from his body.
It is stated that dead body of deceased was taken to Hedgewar Hospital and later post mortem on the dead body was conducted in GTB Hospital.
It is stated that respondent no.1 is the driver of the offending truck, respondent no.2 is owner and it was insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.

2. WS was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 wherein it is stated that truck no.HR-38W-1670 was being driven by respondent no.1 with full care and caution without any rash and negligence when accident occurred on 24.05.2023.
It is stated that no guard/helper was present at the MACT No.383/2023 SHAILENDER
SHAILENDER

It is pleaded that there is no fault on the part of respondent no.1 and 2 as there was no violation of the traffic rules on the part of the driver of the vehicle.
It is further pleaded that respondent no. 1 was having valid DL at the time of accident and also has a great experience to drive the commercial vehicle.
Other averments of the DAR have been denied.

3. In the WS filed by R3 it is stated that injured himself was allegedly working on the flyover unmindful of the oncoming traffic rashly and negligently without any indicator and warning and was solely instrumental in causing the accident.

R3 took all the pleas in terms of section 149 of M.V.
Act and defence u/s 170 of the Act.
It is stated that vehicle no. HR-38W-1670 was insured in the name of M/s Ahmedabad Roadlines Pvt. Ltd. vide policy no.130422323340004302 valid for the period from 14.03.2023 to 13.06.2024.
It is denied that accident took place in the manner as mentioned by the petitioners.
4. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed on 31.10.2023:

OPP (2)Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so to what extent and from whom?
OPP (3)Relief.

Issue No.1 7.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

However during cross examination PW2 admitted that FIR has been lodged on his statement.
He admitted that at the time of accident work of construction was conducted at Surya Nagar red light where flyover has been constructed.
Witness also admitted that at the time of accident deceased was doing welding job of gatters (iron rods).

During cross examination by ld. counsel for R1 and R2, witness stated that he was at the distance of 3 to 4 meters from the place of accident and at the time of accident deceased was working on a pillar.
PW2 stated that he was very much there at the time of accident.

Testimony of PW2 who is eye witness to the accident in question coupled with record of criminal case in the opinion of this Tribunal is sufficient to establish that deceased died due to rash and MACT No.383/2023 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER Page 5 MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 17:11:14 +0530 negligent driving of offending truck bearing registration no.HR38W-1670 driven by respondent no.1.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 11. In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 12.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Kapil Kumar.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.

These issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:

4 (i) additions/ deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
MACT No.383/2023

The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
14.
The petitioner (PW1) in her evidence has proved copy of Aadhar Card and High School certificate of deceased Kapil Kumar as Ex.PW1/B.
Perusal of Aadhar Card as well as certificate-cum-mark sheet of high school certificate of deceased Ex.PW1/B shows that his date of birth was 13.04.2000.
These documents in the opinion of this Tribunal are conclusive proof of age of deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (24.05.2023) was 22 years 11 months.

Assessment of Income of deceased :
15.

Petitioner (PW1) in her deposition stated that her deceased MACT No.383/2023 by SHAILENDER Page 8 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 17:11:40 +0530 husband was a skilled welder and doing private job in Delhi and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
She deposed that deceased was single bread earning member of the family and whole family dependent only on the deceased.
She deposed that due to death of deceased, petitioners have suffered great pain, mental agony and financial loss.
During cross- examination though PW1 stated that her husband was a welder however he has not taken any training of said work.
16. No documentary evidence has been placed on record by the petitioners to prove the profession and income of the deceased.

There can hardly be any dispute with regard to place of accident being Delhi or UP when FIR in this case has been registered at PS Vivek Vihar of Delhi and duly investigated and accused/respondent no.1 has been prosecuted in that case in respect of same accident.

In view of such circumstances this Tribunal is of considered view that once accident is proved to have taken place within the jurisdiction of Delhi, therefore minimum wags of unskilled worker at Delhi would be assessed for the purpose of notional income of the deceased which was Rs.17,234/- per month.

This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
I have gone through entire material available on record.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
8.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 12.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (24.05.2023) was 22 years 11 months.
In view of such circumstances this Tribunal is of considered view that once accident is proved to have taken place within the jurisdiction of Delhi, therefore minimum wags of unskilled worker at Delhi would be assessed for the purpose of notional income of the deceased which was Rs.17,234/- per month.
As held above, deceased was 22 years 11 months of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
In view of the above, multiplier of 18 has to be applied against the age bracket of 21 to 25 years to determine the compensation.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)
